questions.explain: Short-term is verbatim recent turns bounded by token budget (single-digit ms); long-term is distilled summaries/facts/preferences retrieved by relevance (tens of ms). Prompt order: system → long-term → short-term → current message.
options: They are identical; the names are interchangeable
Short-term is in Redis and long-term in SQL Server by requirement

questions.explain: On session close the background worker summarizes the conversation, extracts atomic facts as JSON, deduplicates via vector search (bumping importance instead of duplicating), and embeds everything — never in the chat request path.
options: Summarize, extract facts, deduplicate via vector search, and embed — as a background job on session close
Store every turn verbatim in long-term memory
Ask the user to pick which memories to keep
Run inside the chat request before responding

questions.explain: Recall scores 0.7 × semantic similarity + 0.3 × importance, where cosine distance d in [0,2] converts to similarity as (1 − d/2); returned memories get recall_count, last_recalled_at, and importance bumps.
options: Pure cosine similarity with no other factors
Importance alone, ignoring semantics
Recency alone — newest memories always win
0.7 × semantic similarity + 0.3 × importance, with reinforcement on recall
questions.q: How does usp_recall_memories rank long-term memories?

questions.explain: A nightly job multiplies importance by 0.99 for memories unrecalled in 30 days; contradictions mark the old memory superseded rather than deleting it; decayed trivia (importance < 0.05, never recalled) is pruned.
options: Memories are kept forever with no changes
Nightly importance decay (×0.99), contradiction supersession instead of deletion, and pruning of decayed trivia
All memories are deleted after 30 days
Decay applies only to summaries, never to facts
